examples.title: LED current limiter
examples.objective: Calculate the DC current and resistor dissipation for a 5 V source, 330 Ω resistor, and red LED.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: starter project validates and produces a bounded analytical DC result
examples.safetyNote: Educational low-voltage model only. Do not use the result as a physical-product, thermal, mains, or regulatory safety approval.

examples.title: Two-LED polarity indicator
examples.objective: Use red and green LEDs in opposite orientations, each with a 330 Ω series resistor, to indicate the polarity of a signed 5 V DC source.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: catalogue anti-parallel LEDs change with source polarity
examples.safetyNote: Ideal educational model using generic LEDs with nominal 2.0 V and 2.1 V forward drops. It omits reverse breakdown, tolerance, thermal behavior, ratings, and physical hardware validation.

examples.title: Unloaded DC voltage divider
examples.objective: Calculate unloaded output voltage, branch current, and total power for a 9 V, 1 kΩ / 2 kΩ divider.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: a documented voltage divider produces bounded DC values
examples.safetyNote: Educational low-voltage unloaded model only. A connected load changes the result; do not use it for a physical-product, thermal, mains, or regulatory safety approval.

examples.title: 5 V pushbutton LED with pull-down
examples.objective: Model the catalogue pushbutton LED circuit with a 5 V ideal source, a normally-open series button, a 330 Ω LED resistor, a 10 kΩ pull-down, and a red LED.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: catalogue pushbutton LED stays off until pressed and includes its pull-down
examples.safetyNote: Ideal low-voltage educational model only. It omits switch bounce, component tolerances and ratings, thermal effects, physical breadboard mapping, and hardware safety qualification.

examples.title: Latching LED switch
examples.objective: Model an SPDT switch that selects an illuminated or off state for a low-voltage LED circuit.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: catalogue latching SPDT switch selects a defined LED state
examples.safetyNote: Ideal educational low-voltage model only. It omits switch contact resistance/bounce, part tolerances and ratings, thermal effects, and physical hardware validation.

verification.engine: Analytical ideal latching SPDT LED switch

examples.title: 9 V LED current limiter
examples.objective: Calculate current and resistor dissipation for a 9 V source, 470 Ω resistor, and red LED.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: released examples carry a native project, acceptance test, safety scope, and supported result
examples.safetyNote: Educational low-voltage model only. Confirm actual LED limits, resistor wattage, supply tolerance, and heat before building hardware.

examples.title: 5 V parallel resistor load
examples.objective: Solve a 5 V source feeding a 1 kΩ series resistor and two 1 kΩ parallel load resistors; report midpoint voltage and source current.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: parallel resistor load example has a reproducible DC operating point
examples.safetyNote: Educational low-voltage ideal DC model only. Check real resistor power ratings, supply tolerance, heat, and wiring before hardware use.

examples.title: First-order RC step response
examples.objective: Calculate the ideal 5 V step response of a 1 kΩ resistor charging a 100 µF capacitor from zero initial voltage; report time constant and sampled voltage/current.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: single-pole RC step response reports time constant and analytic samples
examples.safetyNote: Educational ideal low-voltage transient model only. It omits parasitics, source impedance, tolerances, leakage, dielectric effects, and component ratings; verify real parts before hardware use.

examples.title: First-order RL step response
examples.objective: Calculate the ideal 5 V step response of a 100 Ω resistor and 100 mH inductor from zero initial current; report time constant and sampled current/voltage.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: single-pole RL step response reports current rise and inductor voltage
examples.safetyNote: Educational ideal low-voltage transient model only. It omits parasitics, source impedance, tolerances, magnetic saturation, thermal effects, and component ratings; verify real parts before hardware use.

examples.title: 12 V LED current limiter
examples.objective: Calculate ideal LED current and resistor dissipation for a 12 V source, 2.2 kΩ resistor, and 2.0 V red LED.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: 12 V LED limiter example calculates the documented current
examples.safetyNote: Educational ideal low-voltage model only. Confirm the actual LED forward voltage/current rating, resistor wattage, supply tolerance and heat before hardware use.

examples.title: 3.3 V LED current limiter
examples.objective: Calculate ideal LED current and resistor dissipation for a 3.3 V source, 150 Ω resistor, and 2.0 V red LED.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: 3.3 V LED limiter example calculates the documented current
examples.safetyNote: Educational ideal low-voltage model only. Actual LED forward voltage and supply tolerance change current; verify resistor rating, heat and LED limits before building.

examples.title: 9 V divider 3 kΩ / 1 kΩ
examples.objective: Calculate the unloaded output voltage and current for a 9 V source and 3 kΩ / 1 kΩ divider.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: 3 kΩ / 1 kΩ divider example calculates output voltage
examples.safetyNote: Educational low-voltage unloaded model only. A connected load changes the output; do not use as product or regulatory design approval.

examples.title: 12 V parallel resistor load
examples.objective: Solve a 12 V source, 1 kΩ series resistor, and 2 kΩ / 3 kΩ parallel loads; report midpoint voltage and source current.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: 12 V parallel load example solves its midpoint and source current
examples.safetyNote: Educational ideal low-voltage DC model only. Check real resistor power ratings, heat, supply tolerance and wiring before hardware use.

examples.title: RC charge and discharge
examples.objective: Calculate the ideal 5 V, 1 kΩ, 100 µF response with an SPDT switch selecting charge or discharge; report the 0.1 s time constant and voltage at one time constant.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: SPDT RC example calculates charging and discharging at one time constant
examples.safetyNote: Ideal low-voltage educational model only. Generic components, switch resistance, tolerances, leakage, ratings, physical breadboard layout, and PCB footprints are not verified. Discharge assumes a previously charged capacitor at the source voltage.

examples.title: RC low-pass frequency response
examples.objective: Calculate the ideal sinusoidal steady-state response of a 1 kΩ / 100 µF RC low-pass filter at 0.1×, 1×, and 10× cutoff and verify 1/√2 gain at cutoff.
examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: RC low-pass response uses the calculated cutoff and attenuates above it
examples.safetyNote: Ideal educational frequency-domain model only. Generic components have no verified physical ratings, tolerances, parasitics, exact manufacturer BOM, hole-level breadboard mapping, or PCB footprints. It is not hardware or manufacturing guidance.

verification.engine: Analytical first-order RC low-pass frequency response

examples.title: RC high-pass frequency response

examples.acceptanceTest: tests/core.test.mjs: RC high-pass response uses the calculated cutoff and attenuates below it
examples.safetyNote: Ideal educational frequency-domain model only. Generic components have no verified physical ratings, tolerances, parasitics, exact manufacturer BOM, hole-level breadboard mapping, or PCB footprints. It is not hardware or manufacturing guidance.

examples.safetyNote: Ideal educational frequency-domain model only. Generic components have no verified physical ratings, tolerances, parasitics, exact manufacturer BOM, hole-level breadboard mapping, or PCB footprints. It is not hardware or manufacturing guidance.
